*** Add File: D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/frontend-flows/04-password-reset.md
+# Flow 04: Password recovery and reset
+
+Status: initial draft; not approved; owner decisions OPEN  
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda)  
+Mode: specification only; no implementation or delivery evidence  
+Authority: [shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md), then latest owner answers; retained [SPEC-001](../specifications/SPEC-001_dubbed_mvp.md) and [BR-001](../business-requirements/BR-001_custom_video_dubbing.md) apply only where the shared contract has not replaced them
+
+## 1. Purpose and boundary
+
+This flow lets a person who owns an email/password identity request password recovery by email and set a new password after valid confirmation.
+
+The flow must:
+
+- work in English and Russian on desktop and phone;
+- begin from Flow 02 sign-in or a reset entry received by email;
+- never create an account, finish an unverified registration, or link login methods;
+- never infer ownership from an email match alone;
+- finish at the post-reset authentication state selected in OPEN-04;
+- preserve a validated return intent without bypassing authentication.
+
+Google sign-in remains available in Flow 02. Explicit ownership-verified linking belongs to Flow 05. Registration and email verification belong to Flow 03.
+
+This document does not select a delivery provider, reset link versus code, secret lifetime, password policy, automatic sign-in, or session-revocation policy.
+
+## 2. Entry and exit
+
+### Entry
+
+- **Forgot password?** from email/password sign-in, optionally carrying a validated return intent.
+- Direct reset entry from the email mechanism selected in OPEN-01.
+- **Request another email** from an expired, used, invalid, or failed reset state.
+- Browser reload, Back, or Forward while the user is in a recoverable state.
+
+### Exit
+
+| State | Exit |
+|---|---|
+| Request cancelled | Flow 02 sign-in; no email is sent by cancellation. |
+| Request accepted | Stay in this flow and show the email-next-step state selected by OPEN-01 and OPEN-05. |
+| Reset cancelled before submission | Flow 02 sign-in; no password change. |
+| Reset succeeds | Destination and session effect are OPEN-04. |
+| Reset proof is expired, used, invalid, or revoked | Recovery state with **Request another email** and **Back to sign in**. |
+
+No upload, project, credit, recording, result, or linking state is created or mutated by this flow.
+
+## 3. Design application
+
+Both requested design skills are applied as analysis constraints, not owner approval.
+
+- Treat this as a sparse product form, not a marketing page or dashboard.
+- Use the confirmed light rehearsal-room direction: white/light-gray surfaces, readable black text, flat fills, and no gradients, glows, decorative art, or fake product data.
+- Use a compact top header with the Dubbed wordmark/home action, language control, and an appropriate sign-in/back action; never add a permanent sidebar.
+- Keep one narrow reading column and one visible primary action per state. A bordered panel is optional; exact geometry is OPEN-07.
+- Labels stay above fields. Placeholders do not replace labels.
+- Use red only for an actionable error and never as the sole error signal.
+- Use no security illustration, lock icon card, success confetti, or ornamental status badge.
+- Exact font, sizes, colors, radii, widths, spacing, routes, and motion remain OPEN-07 and must be resolved once for the shared authentication shell.
+
+## 4. Screen anatomy
+
+### 4.1 Shared authentication header
+
+- Dubbed wordmark/home action.
+- English/Russian language control.
+- **Back to sign in** when it is a valid next action.
+- No account/project navigation is assumed for an unauthenticated visitor.
+- Behavior when an already authenticated user enters the flow follows OPEN-04.
+
+Changing language must update visible copy, labels, errors, instructions, and accessible names without clearing typed email or password fields.
+
+### 4.2 Request reset email
+
+Required content:
+
+- title: **Reset your password** / **Сброс пароля**;
+- concise instruction to enter the account email;
+- visible **Email** / **Электронная почта** label;
+- one email field with browser autofill support;
+- primary action: **Send reset email** / **Отправить письмо для сброса**;
+- secondary action: **Back to sign in** / **Вернуться ко входу**.
+
+The form normalizes only what the shared identity contract explicitly permits. It must not silently rewrite an address into a different identity.
+
+Disclosure for unknown, Google-only, disabled, or unverified identities is OPEN-05. Until resolved, no copy may claim that an account exists or does not exist.
+
+### 4.3 Request accepted / check email
+
+This state explains the next action without claiming delivery before the logical service accepts the request.
+
+Required responsibilities:
+
+- state which mailbox was targeted only to the disclosure level allowed by OPEN-05;
+- explain the link-or-code action selected by OPEN-01;
+- provide **Resend** only under the retry/cooldown contract selected in OPEN-06;
+- provide **Use a different email** and **Back to sign in**;
+- never display the reset secret in application UI or diagnostics;
+- never claim a real email arrived when a mock service only simulated acceptance.
+
+Exact countdown, cooldown, rate-limit copy, address masking, and whether the state is identical for unknown addresses are OPEN.
+
+### 4.4 Confirm reset artifact
+
+The screen receives the reset proof chosen in OPEN-01:
+
+- a link-delivered proof that can be inspected without re-entering a code;
+- a manually entered code associated with an email/request context; or
+- both, only if the owner explicitly selects both.
+
+Do not render the new-password form until the service reports that the proof is currently eligible for reset. While inspecting, show the stable form frame with a plain loading status and no shimmer.
+
+Possible authoritative states:
+
+- `valid` — permit password entry;
+- `expired` — do not permit mutation; offer another email;
+- `used` — do not permit mutation; offer sign-in and another email;
+- `invalid` or `revoked` — do not permit mutation; offer another email;
+- `temporarily_unavailable` — keep the proof context in memory, show Retry, and do not relabel it invalid.
+
+Whether these states share security-neutral copy is part of OPEN-05. The proof lifetime and single-use rules are OPEN-02.
+
+### 4.5 Set new password
+
+Required controls:
+
+- **New password** / **Новый пароль**;
+- **Confirm new password** / **Подтвердите новый пароль**;
+- separate show/hide controls with persistent accessible names;
+- primary action: **Set new password** / **Установить новый пароль**;
+- secondary action: **Cancel** / **Отмена**.
+
+Password managers and paste must work. The interface must not log, retain, translate, or expose either password value.
+
+The exact minimum/maximum length, allowed characters, composition rules, breached-password handling, and strength guidance are OPEN-03. The client and authoritative service must ultimately present one consistent policy. Matching confirmation is required before a successful submission, but must not be described as the full password policy.
+
+### 4.6 Reset success
+
+Required content:
+
+- one unambiguous success statement;
+- the next action selected in OPEN-04;
+- no password value, reset secret, account metadata, project data, or balance data;
+- no claim that all devices were signed out unless the service confirms that result.
+
+Automatic sign-in, sign-in again, current-device continuity, and revocation of other sessions remain OPEN-04.
+
+## 5. Transitions and recovery
+
+### 5.1 Main request path
+
+1. User opens password recovery from Flow 02.
+2. User enters an email and activates **Send reset email**.
+3. The client prevents duplicate local submission while the request is pending.
+4. The request service returns an authoritative result.
+5. On accepted request, show the check-email state governed by OPEN-01 and OPEN-05.
+6. No account session, registration, link, project, or credit state changes yet.
+
+### 5.2 Main reset path
+
+1. User returns with the proof selected by OPEN-01.
+2. The client asks the service to inspect eligibility.
+3. Valid proof opens the new-password form.
+4. User enters and confirms a password under the future OPEN-03 policy.
+5. The reset service performs one authoritative mutation.
+6. Success applies the session behavior selected in OPEN-04 and consumes or invalidates the proof according to OPEN-02.
+
+### 5.3 Expired, used, invalid, and revoked proofs
+
+- Never submit a password mutation after the service reports an ineligible proof.
+- Keep the reason distinguishable in logical state even if OPEN-05 later requires shared public copy.
+- Offer **Request another email**; do not automatically send one.
+- **Back to sign in** remains available.
+- Retrying inspection after a transport failure is not the same as requesting another email.
+
+### 5.4 Resend and repeated requests
+
+- Resend uses the explicit address/request context allowed by OPEN-05.
+- A resend action must show pending, accepted, cooldown, rate-limited, and unavailable states honestly.
+- No countdown or retry interval is specified before OPEN-06.
+- The relationship between old and new proofs is OPEN-02; do not assume both remain valid or that the newer request revokes the older one.
+
+### 5.5 Service and validation failures
+
+- Invalid email shape: attach a concise error to the email field and focus it on submission.
+- Password confirmation mismatch: attach an error to confirmation without clearing either field.
+- Password policy rejection: present the authoritative unmet rule without echoing the password.
+- Request/reset unavailable: keep safe typed fields, show Retry, and do not report success.
+- Rate limit: show an actionable retry state only if the service supplies a safe retry time; exact behavior is OPEN-06.
+- Proof expires between inspection and submit: preserve no password after leaving the form; show expired recovery and another-email actions.
+- Concurrent/double submit: only one authoritative result may win; never show two success states or retry a mutation blindly.
+
+### 5.6 Reload, Back, Forward, and interruption
+
+- Reload on the request form returns to a usable request form and never sends an email automatically.
+- Reload on check-email reconstructs only non-secret state the chosen contract permits and never claims a resend occurred.
+- Reload on reset entry re-inspects the proof; cached `valid` state is insufficient.
+- Reload during submission checks the authoritative result before allowing another mutation.
+- Back/Forward after success must not restore an actionable password form.
+- Password fields and confirmation are cleared on reload, route exit, expiry, success, and cancellation.
+- Exact handling/storage of a link secret or code is blocked by OPEN-01 and the later security design; no local-storage behavior is approved here.
+
+## 6. Account and session impact
+
+- Password recovery does not create a new account or grant welcome credits.
+- It does not mark an unverified password registration complete; Flow 03 owns email verification and completion.
+- It does not attach Google to an email/password identity or merge libraries/balances; Flow 05 owns explicit verified linking.
+- A matching Google email alone is never authority to reset, create, or link a password credential.
+- Behavior for Google-only, unverified, disabled, deleted, or nonexistent identities is OPEN-05.
+- Existing-session revocation and the post-success session are OPEN-04.
+- A preserved return intent may be used only after the selected authentication requirement succeeds.
+
+## 7. Responsive, keyboard, and accessibility behavior
+
+### Desktop
+
+- Use the shared compact top header and a single-column form region.
+- Keep instruction, fields, errors, and actions in one reading order.
+- Do not place unrelated product promotion beside the recovery form.
+
+### Phone
+
+- Keep 16–20px outer margins as a design target, subject to OPEN-07.
+- Controls and icon buttons need at least 44px touch targets.
+- The form is full-width within the page margin; no horizontal page scroll.
+- Keep the primary action visible after the software keyboard without fixed overlays hiding fields or errors.
+- Do not replace the header with a sidebar or multi-level account menu.
+
+### Keyboard and assistive technology
+
+- Logical order: header, title/instructions, fields, field help/errors, primary action, secondary actions.
+- Enter submits only the current eligible form; it never triggers Resend from an unrelated state.
+- Visible focus is required for every interactive element.
+- On validation failure, focus the first invalid field and associate each message programmatically.
+- Announce pending, accepted, expired, used, unavailable, and success state changes without stealing focus repeatedly.
+- Show/hide controls expose current state and do not move focus or change field content.
+- Errors use text plus structure/iconography; color alone is insufficient.
+
+## 8. Logical service boundary
+
+Names below describe responsibilities, not approved endpoints or implementation files.
+
+| Logical operation | Inputs | Required result categories |
+|---|---|---|
+| `requestPasswordReset` | email, locale, validated return intent if supported | accepted, invalid input, cooldown/rate limit, unavailable |
+| `inspectResetProof` | proof context selected by OPEN-01 | valid, expired, used, invalid, revoked, unavailable |
+| `submitNewPassword` | eligible proof, new password, request/revision context | success, policy rejection, mismatch/conflict, expired, used, invalid/revoked, rate limit, unavailable |
+| `resolveSession` | current session context | authenticated, anonymous, expired, unavailable |
+| `applyResetSessionPolicy` | successful reset result | outcome selected by OPEN-04, or explicit failure |
+
+The service layer is centralized and interchangeable, as required by the shared contract. Zustand may coordinate view state but is not an authority for proof eligibility, password mutation, email delivery, or session revocation.
+
+### Mock-truth boundary
+
+A mock may deterministically simulate every result above, including delay, expiry, used proof, policy rejection, and unavailable service.
+
+A mock cannot prove:
+
+- that any email was delivered;
+- ownership of a mailbox;
+- reset-proof entropy, expiry, revocation, replay resistance, or single-use enforcement;
+- password hashing, breached-password checks, rate limiting, abuse prevention, or account-enumeration resistance;
+- session invalidation across browsers/devices;
+- provider uptime, sender reputation, or deliverability.
+
+UI checks against a mock must be labeled simulation, not backend, provider, or security evidence.
+
+## 9. Acceptance criteria
+
+All criteria are unexecuted. `BLOCKED` means an owner/security decision is still required.
+
+- [ ] **AC-04-01 Request form:** English/Russian request UI accepts an email, exposes pending/failure states, supports keyboard use, and never mutates account state on cancellation. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-05/OPEN-06 for disclosure and retry behavior.
+- [ ] **AC-04-02 Email next step:** accepted request shows accurate instructions and explicit resend/different-email/sign-in actions without claiming mock delivery. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-01, OPEN-05, and OPEN-06.
+- [ ] **AC-04-03 Proof lifecycle:** valid, expired, used, invalid, revoked, and unavailable proof states produce the specified safe transition and never reuse cached eligibility. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-01/OPEN-02.
+- [ ] **AC-04-04 Password form:** password and confirmation fields work with paste/password managers, accessible show/hide controls, mismatch handling, and consistent policy feedback without retaining secrets. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-03.
+- [ ] **AC-04-05 Successful reset:** exactly one authoritative password mutation is represented as success; account creation, registration completion, and linking do not occur. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-02/OPEN-04 for proof consumption and session effects.
+- [ ] **AC-04-06 Interruption:** reload, Back/Forward, transport failure, duplicate submission, and expiry-between-inspection-and-submit never fabricate delivery, validity, mutation, or session revocation.
+- [ ] **AC-04-07 Separation:** Google-only and unverified-registration cases cannot silently create/link a password identity or bypass Flow 03/05. `BLOCKED` on OPEN-05 for visible recovery behavior.
+- [ ] **AC-04-08 Responsive access:** desktop and phone layouts preserve one clear action, labels above fields, 44px phone targets, visible focus, announced status/errors, and no sidebar or horizontal page scroll. Exact visual comparison is `BLOCKED` on OPEN-07.
+- [ ] **AC-04-09 Evidence truth:** mock verification is reported as simulation; real email, backend security, session revocation, and cross-device behavior remain unverified until production-capable dependencies and evidence exist.
+
+## 10. Verification plan — not executed
+
+- Component/state checks for request, check-email, proof inspection, password form, and success states in EN/RU.
+- Keyboard-only walkthrough: focus order, Enter behavior, error focus, show/hide controls, Resend isolation, and Back to sign in.
+- Responsive visual review at representative desktop and 390px phone widths after OPEN-07 is resolved.
+- Mock contract cases for accepted request, invalid input, cooldown/rate limit, unavailable request, valid/expired/used/invalid/revoked proof, policy rejection, conflict, and successful reset.
+- Navigation/reload cases for request form, check-email, reset entry, in-flight submit, success history, and preserved validated return intent.
+- Boundary checks that no password or reset proof reaches Zustand persistence, analytics, visible diagnostics, URL logging, or error text under the final OPEN-01 security design.
+- Integration checks with a real backend/email provider for delivery, ownership proof, expiry, replay/single-use behavior, rate limits, password policy, and session invalidation; these cannot run from the current frontend-only specification.
+- Target-browser/device checks remain required before claiming support in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Android Chrome, or iPhone Safari.
+
+Record command or method, result, environment, date, revision/dirty boundary, fixture or account class, and evidence location. No check has been run for this draft.
+
+## 11. Open decisions and dependencies
+
+| ID | Decision/dependency | Why it blocks |
+|---|---|---|
+| OPEN-01 | Email contains a reset link, a code, or both. | Determines entry, fields, copy, deep-link/reload behavior, and proof handling. |
+| OPEN-02 | Proof lifetime, single-use/replay rule, resend effect on older proofs, and expiry semantics. | Determines expired/used behavior and authoritative service contract. |
+| OPEN-03 | Exact password policy and user-visible guidance. | Determines validation, copy, disabled/error states, and success eligibility. |
+| OPEN-04 | Post-reset automatic sign-in versus sign-in again; current and other-session revocation. | Determines success exit, active-session entry, and security acceptance. |
+| OPEN-05 | Disclosure policy for unknown, Google-only, unverified, disabled, and deleted identities; address masking. | Determines account-enumeration behavior and every request/recovery message. |
+| OPEN-06 | Resend cooldown, request/reset rate limits, retry timing, and lockout behavior. | Determines controls, countdowns, errors, and abuse-resistance verification. |
+| OPEN-07 | Shared auth routes, exact type/tokens/geometry, and any motion. | Determines visual acceptance without authorizing a per-flow design system. |
+| DEP-01 | Flow 02 sign-in and validated return-intent contract. | Owns entry, cancellation, and sign-in destination. |
+| DEP-02 | Flow 03 registration/email verification. | Prevents reset from silently completing unverified registration. |
+| DEP-03 | Flow 05 explicit account linking. | Prevents email matching from merging identities. |
+| DEP-04 | Real backend identity/session service and email provider. | Required for delivery, proof security, password mutation, and session evidence. |
+
+Questions OPEN-01, OPEN-02, and OPEN-04 were sent to the Orchestrator first. OPEN-03, OPEN-05, and OPEN-06 remain queued owner/security choices; no recommended option is an approved requirement.
*** End Patch";
const r = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(r);
